text:
The physician may be found liable if the cervical springing was done without a documented pre-manipulation screen for vertebrobasilar or cervical arterial dysfunction, despite red flags (age 78, severe unexplained neck pain, recent prolonged overhead neck posture), and without informed consent that disclosed stroke risk. The plaintiff would also need expert testimony that the manipulation more likely than not caused or contributed to the posterior-circulation event, such as a vertebral artery dissection, because timing alone (four hours) does not establish causation. If a documented screen was performed or the event was a coincidental stroke, liability is much less likely.

CONFIDENCE: 70
